FUNERAL POLICY RACKET

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A funeral policy provider rips of clients - pocketing hundreds of thousands of rands - we investigate

Unique Selling Point:
WHY WILL VIEWERS LOVE IT?
 UNDERCOVER STING
 A ROYAL ROGUE TAKING ADVANTAGE OF PEOPLE AROUND DEATH – sies man!
 A CONFRONT DURBAN STYLE – it’s gonna be great J

Summary:
It’s a straight forward scam. There’s a bad guy taking people for a ride. We can prove it. There are case studies ready to go on camera. And an insider. What’s worse – these people are being taken for a ride at the worst possible time – when someone has just died!

Further information:
FUNERAL POLICY FRAUD



THE SCAM:
You buy a funeral policy from Churches of Africa – cover say for R30000 – this is would cover the cost of the funeral and a cashback payout of say R10k. But when your loved one dies, you find out you’re not covered for everything funeral related and if you’re lucky there’s a cashback of say R3000.

HOW DOES THE SCAM WORK:
Churches of Africa collects R150 per month – but they only cover the client with the underwriters for R10000 and not the R30000. They only pay a portion of the client monthly subscription fee over to the underwriter and pocket the rest. WE CAN PROVE THIS!
1. With paper work done at application.
2. We call the current underwriters and confirm.
3. We do a sting – catching them out with our own policy.

An opposition company has already done this with a list of clients and can confirm the scam already.

WHY SHOULD WE CARE:
It may sound small but if your scooping R100 off every client and you have 2000 clients – that’s R200 000 in your pocket every month!
1. THAT’s DODGE.
2. IT’S ILLEGAL TO COLLECT MONEY IF YOU ARE NOT REGISTERED FINANCIAL SERVICES PROVIDER – WHICH THIS COMPANY IS NOT



CASE STUDIES
1. Mbuso R Msomi, 620605584084, took a Coffin plan + R 10 000 and upon calling KGA, discovered that they were only covered for R 10 000- Contact Rose(wife) 063 350 3147

CONFIRMED WITH UNDERWRITER
Beryl Vertuin, 5605170125083
Inception date: 2018-09-01
Insurance Cover: R10 000

3. Venketamma P Sathoo, 5912280138083, took a Policy from COA in 2016 and upon calling KGA, discovered that they only received activation of her policy in 2018- Contact Vasha (Daughter) 084 407 7363/ 065 949 2133
CONFIRMED WITH UNDERWRITER
Venketamma P Sathoo, 5912280138083
Inception date: 2014-10-01
Insurance Cover: R10 000

UNDERCOVER
We’ve sent in two operatives – both have signed up and paid and both have not been loaded with the underwriter – so we’ve paid three premiums so far and are not covered.

EXTRA BUDGET


INTERVIEWS
 Insider on camera that used to work that can testify to money laundering
 Opposition Company – how they realized the company was doing cooking the books and cheating clients
 Insurance Crime Bureau – why it’s illegal what is going down
 CASE STUDIES x 3
 EITHER THE UNDERWRITER KGA LIFE OR THE FINANCIAL Financial SECTOR CONDUCT AUTHORITY – will confirm tomorrow.

PLAN IS TO SHOOT MONDAY & TUESDAY IN DURBAN


Extra Budget Items:
** TRAVEL & ACCOMODATION DURBAN
** PREMIUMS – R540 (3 x R180)
** UNDERCOVER INVESTIGATION – AGENT SENT IN THREE TIMES - R4500

OR WE CAN AGREE ON INVESTIGATIVE RATE AND I’ll COVER THE INVESTIGATION COSTS

Script:


STRUCTURE

VO: Death can be expensive. While funerals are not cheap, insurance policies are easy to come by, in an Industry that’s become increasingly cut throat.

LINK: Funeral Cover is the solution many people look to, to ease the financial burden and admin of death – providing a policy that will pay for the funeral and in many cases a lump sum pay out.

GARTH: It's a massive business worldwide, it's it's worth billions, and I think that's exactly what attracts criminals and fraudsters to the industry. //INT1M1

VO: Insurance Crime Bureau CEO, Garth de Klerk explains that while there are credible operators – there are just as many dodgy ones, who break the rules to maximise profits.

One of these alleged companies is Churches of Africa, based in Durban, owned by Pastor Emmanuel Devalingham.

PASTOR: // My thing is to serve our people with excellence, with honesty, integrity// CLIP 50 00:03:20:08

VO: The company presents itself as an Executive Funeral Home and Burial Fund. We interviewed Pastor Emmanuel at an office being renovated.

PASTOR: the reason that I started the churches of Africa was to create a safe haven so that our people can be protected from being exploited during the time of a funeral //CLIP 50 00:00:27:20

VO: But let’s just get the record straight up front. Churches of Africa or COA as it’s known is not a registered funeral home, nor is it a registered Financial Services Provider, nor is it a registered insurer. COA is an agent that sells policies. That is it.

Basically funeral insurance should work like this:

Policies are underwritten by registered insurance companies – premiums are paid to the insurance company, either directly or via a sales agent.

By the Pastor’s own estimation COA has roughly 2000 clients. Most who fall in the lower income bracket, in and around Durban. Rose Hutchinson signed up in 2016.

ROSE to bury a person is very expensive // /I just get a stipend, which is three, four, and that wouldn't cover that are so important to have a policy. INT1 M1

VO: Rose opted for the complete burial package valued at roughly R10 000, plus an additional ten thousand rand in cash– that would essentially give her R20 000 worth of cover at a premium of R100 per month.

But that’s not what she got. Rose’s policy was only registered with the insurer in 2018 for only R10000 - despite paying the premiums to COA since 2016 for what she thought R20000 cover.

MASA: // How does that make you feel?
ROSE: WOW! Very angry, very, very angry. INT2M9
MASA: Do you think you were scammed?
ROSE: yes! Definitely! INT2 M4 // // what Churches of Africa's doing. That's not right. INT2M6

VO: Rose’s neighbour Beryl Vertuin was in the same boat.

BERYL: don't know now what which way // we were on time not one day, so we weren't behind with anythingEND INT2M8

VO: Beryl had been paying for the same COA plan since 2017 – she was only registered with the underwriter in 2018 and also for the half the insured amount she was paying COA for.

GARTH: // the guys stealing the premium from the underwriter, they are taking the risk on a self-insurance basis. // And that's it's an illegal practice. INT1M21

VO: So the Pastor has been collecting premiums and not paying it over to the insurer – this means some clients were not covered with legitimate insurance policies.

Interested to check the Pastor’s sales pitch – we sent in two undercover agents.

UPSOUND UNDERCOVER….REC0020 09.00
PASTOR: The funeral plus R10 000 cash
AGENT: that will be 180 a month
PASTOR nods
REC0020 10.14
PASTOR: the most important plan let me advise you is the casket plan -

VO: The operatives paid for a R180 policy in September and October. There would be a six-month waiting period – as the pastor confirmed in our interview.

PASTOR: we are basically considered as intermediaries working with an underwriter. CLIP 50 00:04:41:11
MASA: those premiums go to for those six months.CLIP 50 00:11:03:26
PASTOR //. Premiums have to go to the underwriters // CLIP 50 00:11:15:07

VO: That would be correct Pastor, but when we followed up with the underwriter we learnt that no cover had been registered for either of the operatives.

PASTOR: Well, I need to. I need to. I need to investigate this myself. I need to look into this. I need to speak to our underwriter. CLIP 51 00:02:58:18

VO: We checked our undercover policies with the underwriter again – Clinton McDonald is the CEO of KGA Life.

CLINTON: // we could not find any evidence of that. So that simply means that information was never passed on to us. //

VO: We also asked KGA Life to check Rose and Beryl’s policies.

They confirmed - both clients were only insured for half the cover they signed up for.

Beryl’s cover started with KGA a year after she signed up with COA.

MASA: So OK, for a whole year you were taking this money and pocketing it? CLIP 51 00:08:10:28
PASTOR: No, no. I need to look at it. // for the fact that to do a check as to why the policy was not underwritten. CIP 53 00:08:06:28

VO: Rose’s cover started with KGA two years after she started paying premiums to COA.

MASA: So where did that money go for two years.CLIP51 00:04:26:18
PASTOR: There's definitely something wrong. // there is no way that I am going to allow myself to carry that fact, //CLIP51 00:04:46:20

VO: It seems the pastor has only been underwriting the cash benefit and self-insuring the funeral cover aspect of the policy by pooling premiums.

GARTH: They're double dipping. They are making money from the commission of the sale as well. Then they're making profits, // from provision of a service to the bereaved / NT1M11

VO: Accept you have to be registered with the Department of Health and the Department of HOme Affairs in order to call yourself a legitimate funeral home - which COA is not, by the Pastor’s own admission.

MASA: So you technically are not a funeral home? //CLIP 50 00:01:58:22
PASTOR: Well, the booklet it says I am. In other words, we provide what I was trying to say. They will be said funeral home is that we serve our members personally. //

VO: The Pastor claimed these allegations were the work of his opposition trying to taint his company name.

PASTOR: Opposition looks at us and sees us as a threat by and tries to put this plan in the works so that we could be maybe publicized,CLIP 50 00:22:53:07 -

VO: Carl Dasappa is from SA Funeral Solutions. This company took over some of COA’s clients and became suspicious when they discovered some anomalies with those client policies.

CARL: If you check every 50 and 60 rand policy, you can see it's not underwritten – he can’t dance his way out of that. INT4M1

VO: We checked a sample of 9 clients with KGA – the booklet and the receipts state - UNDERWRITTEN BY KGA Life - they were all on the COA Funeral Benefit Plan - not one of them could be found on the underwriter’s system despite these clients paying premiums to COA.

MASA: How sure accurate?
CLINTON we’re a thousand percent sure that the information // INT1M13

PASTOR: OK, so that is the funeral benefit plan.CLIP 50 00:18:58:15
MASA: And that what does that mean? Does that mean you don't pay the underwriter the premiums? CLIP 50 00:19:05:04
PASTOR: The funeral benefit plan is is a policy where we provide our people with the service. There's no cash attached to it. //CLIP 50 00:19:09:02
MASA: //You should still insure them with your underwriter. They are not insured.CLIP 50 00:20:02:22
PASTOR: OK. On the funeral benefit plan, I need to, but I can agree with that because we roll out the service. In other words. In other words, we pay a service provider. We pay a service provider. Right.CLIP 50 00:20:11:11 // the cremation fees or the burial fees need to be paid, it's paid. // CLIP 54 00:10:18:28 - 00:10:37:04

GARTH: //The people that were paying churches of Africa were under the impression, // that their premium // were being paid to a genuine registered insurer. // that money was incorrectly collected. / NT1M16

VO: Dasappa saw the impact of this first hand when a former COA client died shortly after moving her policy across to his company.

CARL: ///When we submitted the claim, the underwriter had informed us that the client was covered for a third of what they were supposed to be covered. //. INT2M2l

VO: There was a shortfall on the cover because COA underinsured the client - Dasappa’s company absorbed the shortfall and paid out the clients cash back from their own pockets.

CARL: // it’s not the client's fault. They were promised something and they paid the premium. // the burden of that should fallen to them. INT2M3

VO: We confirmed with KGA Life that all of these clients are either under insured or not at all. Conservatively speaking, if the Pastor collects R50 on each of those 2000 policies and “self-insures”- he’s getting in at least R100 000 every month.

PAstor Emmanuel insists that all COA client claims have been paid out and funerals provided - albeit in part from the COA kitty.

PASTOR: // in my mind, I'm not doing anything wrong. To be honest with you, if there's anything that I'm doing that is wrong, I'm ignorant of it. And I need to put it right.CLIP 54 00:05:59:09
MASA : Isn't it a bit strange that 21 years later you're still doing your homework about an industry that you've been in ? CLIP 53 00:18:06:20
PASTOR: // R egulations and laws change all the time. // like I said, maybe I'm not such an intelligent person or a mastermind that has degrees and stuff like that.CLIP 53 00:18:15:04

LINK: // there are rules and regulations – and this is what distinguishes credible operators from those that operate in grey areas who taking chances and treat the law as optional.

VO: While the misrepresentation could seem small, it can have serious consequences for Churches of Africa’s conduct.

GARTH: /It has to be criminally investigated and prosecuted. So there's both ethical and criminal considerations. INT1M18

CUT CARL: But people, the clients that are paying the hard earned money need to be honored. They need to be done right by they need to be justifiably taken care of. They are paying their policies. INT2M7


FUNERAL PROMOS
PROMO1
VO: Even when industries are regulated – there are always chance takers who treat the law as optional – we investigate a funeral cover provider in Durban that’s allegedly been pocketing premiums.


PROMO2
VO: While death is expensive, funeral policy are meant to ease the cost of burial – but one KZN cover provider appears to be profiting by taking premiums, and underinsuring clients - if at all.

PROMO3
VO: We investigate how one Durban-based funeral COVER provider is pocketing clients’ funeral policy premiums, and leaving them under insured if at all – while posing as a legitimate operator.

metadata.Summary: It’s a straight forward scam. There’s a bad guy taking people for a ride. We can prove it. There are case studies ready to go on camera. And an insider. What’s worse – these people are being taken for a ride at the worst possible time – when someone has just died!
metadata.Further information: FUNERAL POLICY FRAUD THE SCAM: You buy a funeral policy from Churches of Africa – cover say for R30000 – this is would cover the cost of the funeral and a cashback payout of say R10k. But when your loved one dies, you find out you’re not covered for everything funeral related and if you’re lucky there’s a cashback of say R3000. HOW DOES THE SCAM WORK: Churches of Africa collects R150 per month – but they only cover the client with the underwriters for R10000 and not the R30000. They only pay a portion of the client monthly subscription fee over to the underwriter and pocket the rest. WE CAN PROVE THIS! 1. With paper work done at application. 2. We call the current underwriters and confirm. 3. We do a sting – catching them out with our own policy. An opposition company has already done this with a list of clients and can confirm the scam already. WHY SHOULD WE CARE: It may sound small but if your scooping R100 off every client and you have 2000 clients – that’s R200 000 in your pocket every month! 1. THAT’s DODGE. 2.
